subject: Renewal: throughput uplift + model swap (long-context + reranker) — reserved pool sizing
messages:
From: Grace Lee <grace.lee@finosystems.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: FinOS Systems Procurement <procurement@finosystems.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning: expected model swap and capacity uplift

Hi Soojin,

We're starting renewal planning for our Dedicated cluster with Redwood. Over the next quarter we'll migrate our ranking pipeline to a new two-stage flow: a 65B long-context encoder (20k tokens) for document retrieval + a lightweight reranker that will score top-K candidates. This increases average tokens per request and raises KV cache pressure.

Current usage: ~8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs, steady-state 40 req/s with average 1.2k tokens. Expected after swap: ~120 req/s steady, average ~6k tokens per highlighted request profile (we still expect many small requests, but large-context jobs will spike).

Ask: for the renewal (contract anniversary in mid-August) we need a recommended reserved capacity plan (GPU count, reserved pools/burst policy), a target throughput guarantee we can commit to our execs, and any suggested configuration (quantization, batching, caching) to control cost while hitting latency SLOs.

Attached a short risk assessment and procurement SOF. Procurement asked for a simple committed capacity number to include in the purchase order.

Thanks — would love an initial SOW-level sizing this week if possible.

Best,
Grace
Head of ML Platforms
FinOS Systems

Attachments: FinOS_RiskAssessment_2026.pdf (pdf), procurement_sof.csv (csv)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Grace Lee <grace.lee@finosystems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: expected model swap and capacity uplift

Hi Grace — thanks for the clear rundown. This helps a lot.

Quick answers up front: we can put together a recommended reserved-capacity proposal and a throughput SLA. To do a tighter sizing we need a couple of datapoints from your side:
- 95th latency target (p95) for the long-context requests — what the product team wants (e.g., 300ms, 500ms, 1s)?
- Expected % of traffic that will be "long-context" vs small requests (rough split will drive batching strategy).
- Whether reranker will run as a synchronous in-line call (adds to tail latency) or in an async batch/sidecar.

Ben (CC) will run a quick modeling exercise and propose pool sizing (primary reserved + burst). I'll follow up with pricing options and a proposed addendum for the renewal term (12 vs 24 months) once we have numbers.

If you want, we can do a 30-min call Friday to walk the SRE/ML folks through the numbers.

— Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Grace Lee <grace.lee@finosystems.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: expected model swap and capacity uplift

Hi Grace / Soojin — I modeled a few realistic mixes based on the numbers you sent. High-level recommendation below (deltas vs your current 8-A100 config):

Assumptions:
- Long-context model ~65B, 20k token window; average token emission per long job ~6k tokens; paraphrase/rerank calls are short (200-400 tokens) but invoked at top-K per query.
- Target p95 latency for interactive workflows: 500ms for small requests, 1.5s for long-context end-to-end (document-stream + rerank).
- We assume ~25% of requests are long-context at peak.

Sizing recommendation (reserved pools):
- Primary reserved pool: 16x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs for steady throughput (handles baseline and most long-context jobs with continuous batching and KV caching).
- Burst pool: 4x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs for short-lived peaks (auto-burst if queue depth > threshold).
- Total committed: 20 A100-equivalent GPUs (adds 12 to your current 8).

Configuration notes:
- Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for document embeddings to reduce token compute on re-reads.
- Use mixed quantization profile for the 65B encoder (Q4/INT8 where safe) to halve memory and allow denser batching.
- Reranker: we recommend running the top-K rerank synchronously but on a smaller model instance to limit added tail latency; alternatively, an async re-score pipeline if your UX allows it.

Throughput SLA proposal:
- Committed throughput guarantee: 120 requests/s (steady-state) across the reserved pools with a 99th percentile fallback policy to burst capacity.
- Latency SLOs: p95 small requests <500ms; p95 end-to-end long-context <1.5s (with documented caveats for 20k-token documents).

Estimated uplift (per-month committed cost) and a 10% committed-term discount for 12-month: I will hand to Soojin and finance for pricing.

Let me know if you want a diagramed pool layout and traffic shaping rules — I can prep that.

— Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Grace Lee <grace.lee@finosystems.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: expected model swap and capacity uplift

Grace — thanks for the patience. Based on Ben's sizing and Soojin's notes we've prepared a commercial proposal:

- Term: 12 months renewal (mid-August start)
- Committed capacity: 20 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (16 primary + 4 burst)
- Throughput guarantee: 120 req/s steady-state across the reserved pools
- Pricing: 10% discount applied to committed capacity vs list for 12-month term; one-time migration/enablement fee (line-item in SOW).
- SLAs: 99.9% uptime on dedicated pool; credits tied to missed uptime/throughput guarantees.

Next steps:
1) Legal addendum (simple capacity addendum + SLA) — Markus will draft and share by EOD Tuesday.
2) SOW and pricing sheet attached for procurement.
3) DocuSign-ready order form once procurement confirms internal PO.

Attachments: redwood_comm_mop_v2.pdf, SOW_FinOS_upgrade.xlsx

Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal planning: expected model swap and capacity uplift

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with our internal expectation. Procurement is OK to proceed on the 12-month commit for 20 GPUs with the stated SLA.

Questions before I sign:
- Can you confirm target start date for reserved capacity (we'd like provisioned and tested one week before mid-August cutover)?
- Can you include an initial migration runbook / rollout checklist in the SOW (we need to validate fallback behavior on day one)?

We accept the pricing and would like the DocuSign link. I've attached the procurement SOF again for your records.

Best,
Grace
Head of ML Platforms, FinOS Systems
